entries.snippet: TVK functionary Aadhav Arjuna has accused Chennai City Police Commissioner A Arun of obstructing party leader Vijay's election campaign in the city. Arjuna alleged that the commissioner pressured local officers, resulting in the disruption of planned rallies in Villivakkam, Anna Nagar, and T Nagar. He highlighted a specific incident where police reduced the approved campaign time in T Nagar from 2pm-6pm to only an hour, despite earlier clearance from the Returning Officer. Arjuna criticized the police's role in altering permissions and claimed such interference did not occur in Trichy or Puducherry, where traffic control measures facilitated campaign activities. He also accused the Chennai police of attempting to restrict Vijay to one constituency and prevent him from accessing key urban areas. Describing the commissioner as "dishonest," Arjuna announced TVK’s intention to escalate the matter to the Chief Electoral Officer and potentially the Election Commission in Delhi, demanding fair treatment and public safety from law enforcement. Commissioner Arun did not respond to media inquiries.
entries.title: City commissioner hindering Vijay's rallies, alleges TVK

entries.snippet:
School Education Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi is contesting for a third consecutive term from the Thiruverumbur assembly constituency, representing the DMK. A sitting MLA since 2016 and a close associate of the party leadership, Mahesh faces a split opposition this time, including AIADMK's former MP P Kumar and TVK’s Navalpattu Viji (alias Vijayakumar), a former DMK member. While Mahesh has historically drawn support from local welfare associations and trade unions in key industrial hubs like BHEL and the Ordnance Factory, this election presents added challenges due to anti-incumbency and internal dissension.

Vijayakumar's entry, especially among youth voters, may fragment votes, though TVK’s internal discontent over his candidacy could limit his impact. NTK's Jallikattu T Rajessh, who polled significantly in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, is also in the fray. Despite Mahesh’s ministerial accomplishments, key promises such as infrastructure upgrades and waste management remain pending. However, with support from Left-leaning unions and urban residents' associations, and his wife Janani Mahesh aiding in rural campaigning, Mahesh remains optimistic about a strong re-election, banking on his government’s broader track record.
entries.title: Anbil Mahesh eyes hat-trick in Thiruverumbur amid split challenge

entries.snippet:
As the nomination deadline for the assembly elections concluded on Monday, candidates from major political parties in the central region of Tamil Nadu actively submitted their nomination papers. In Srirangam, DMK's S Durairaj filed his papers following a procession with party and alliance members. AIADMK's Leema Rose, wife of lottery baron Martin, filed her nomination in Lalgudi. Congress candidate V Lenin Prasad submitted his nomination in the reserved Thuraiyur constituency, accompanied by prominent DMK and Congress leaders. 

In Thiruverumbur, AIADMK's former MP P Kumar and TVK's Navalpattu Viji filed nominations. Pudukkottai district saw nominations from Minister and Thirumayam MLA S Regupathy, Minister Siva Meyyanathan (Alangudi), AIADMK MLA C Vijayabaskar, DMK’s K K Chellapandyan (Viralimalai), and BJP’s Ramachandran (Pudukkottai). In Karur district, DMK candidates from Aravakurichi, Krishnarayapuram, and Kulithalai also filed their nominations. The filings marked the final rush by key candidates across constituencies ahead of the upcoming state assembly elections.
entries.title: Candidates of major parties file papers on last day

entries.snippet:
During a campaign tour across Thanjavur, Perambalur, and Ariyalur districts, Tamil Nadu Deputy Chief Minister Udhayanidhi Stalin criticized AIADMK General Secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami (EPS), sarcastically suggesting that EPS should remain the permanent leader of AIADMK to secure DMK’s electoral victories. Referring to Palaniswami as a “brutal slave,” Udhayanidhi remarked that EPS frequently talks about him, and quipped that it would benefit both DMK and Tamil Nadu if EPS continues leading AIADMK.

Udhayanidhi campaigned in Kunnam for incumbent MLA and Transport Minister S. S. Sivasankar, emphasizing local development. In Thiruvaiyaru, while supporting five-time MLA Durai Chandrasekaran, he urged voters to ensure a larger margin of victory, promising to advocate for Chandrasekaran’s ministerial position if he wins by at least 60,000 to one lakh votes. Udhayanidhi also visited Thiruvidaimaruthur to back incumbent MLA and minister Govi Chezhian.
entries.title: EPS must be permanent AIADMK chief to ensure DMK's win in future: Udhaya

entries.snippet: TVK president and actor Vijay is likely to return to Trichy for another round of campaigning, according to Ku Pa Krishnan, the party's central region in-charge and Lalgudi candidate. Speaking from the TVK office near Gandhi Market, Krishnan addressed several issues including a recent cash seizure from a relative of Vijay. He questioned the legality of the action, emphasizing that searches of private residences require formal summons. Regarding concerns over Vijay’s nomination papers and his decision to contest in two constituencies, Krishnan asserted there were no irregularities and compared the move to decisions made by past leaders like Indira Gandhi and J Jayalalithaa. He concluded by expressing confidence in TVK’s rising public support and projected electoral success.
entries.title: 'Vijay may campaign in Trichy again'

entries.snippet: TVK (Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam) chief Vijay has cancelled his scheduled election campaign in Chennai. The decision was made due to logistical constraints imposed by local authorities. The announcement came on Monday, April 6, 2026.
entries.title: TVK chief Vijay calls off Chennai campaign

entries.snippet:
In the lead-up to the Tamil Nadu state elections, the DMK is focusing on its stronghold in northern Tamil Nadu, which historically provides about one-third of its sitting MLAs. Out of nine districts from Cuddalore to Tiruvannamalai, DMK currently holds 34 seats compared to AIADMK’s 14. Key DMK leaders from the region, such as E V Velu and Duraimurugan, reinforce the party’s grassroots strength and local support. AIADMK, attempting a comeback, is fielding former ministers and relying on alliances like that with PMK to secure Vanniyar votes. However, internal PMK rifts between party founder S Ramadoss and his son Anbumani might dilute AIADMK’s voter base.

The caste composition—particularly among Vanniyars and Dalits—significantly impacts outcomes. DMK benefits from its alliance with VCK to secure Dalit support. Meanwhile, BJP plays a minimal role but could help DMK by drawing minority support through polarization. Actor Vijay’s newly formed TVK and Seeman’s NTK add to the competition but lack organizational strength. DMK also leans on welfare programs like ₹1000 monthly aid to women, while AIADMK criticizes its dynastic politics and seeks to leverage anti-incumbency. Experts believe DMK has the upper hand due to favorable alliances and ground-level support.
entries.title: DMK banks on northern stronghold for return to Fort St George

entries.snippet: On Monday, six Members of Parliament from Tamil Nadu took their oaths as Rajya Sabha members. Among them, three are returning MPs: AIADMK's M Thambidurai, PMK's Anbumani Ramadoss, and DMK's Trichy Siva. The newcomers include Congress's Christopher Manickam, DMK's Constantine Ravindran, and DMDK's L K Sudhish. During the oath-taking, Siva, Anbumani, and Constantine Ravindran swore allegiance to values, while Thambidurai, Sudhish, and Manickam took their oaths in the name of God. A moment of contention arose when Sudhish wore his party shawl during the ceremony and was instructed by Vice-President C P Radhakrishnan to remove it. Sudhish also held up a picture of the late DMDK founder Vijayakant during the proceedings.
entries.title: 6 TN MPs take oath in Rajya Sabha

entries.snippet: On April 6, 2026, AIADMK candidate S P Velumani expressed strong confidence in his electoral success in the Thondamuthur constituency for the upcoming Tamil Nadu Assembly election scheduled on April 23. Speaking boldly, Velumani claimed he would secure victory by a margin of at least one lakh votes. This assertion highlights his optimism regarding his support base and campaign momentum in the region.
entries.title: S P Velumani says he will win by one lakh votes in Thondamuthur

entries.snippet: Posters have surfaced in Mayiladuthurai criticizing MP R Sudha for supporting the nomination of Congress candidate Y N Jamal Muhammad Younoos in the upcoming Tamil Nadu assembly elections. Younoos, a 39-year-old from Thanjavur district, has been nominated to contest from the Mayiladuthurai assembly constituency. Local Congress workers expressed dissatisfaction, claiming Younoos is an outsider with no connection or contribution to the constituency or the party locally. The posters, which appeared in places such as bus stands, railway stations, and government buildings, were published under the name of the 'Mayiladuthurai District Congress Committee All Divisions'. They condemned the leadership’s decision to overlook local candidates. Tamil Nadu Congress Committee’s Mayiladuthurai district president, S Bhanusekar, attributed the backlash to a few disgruntled party members, defending Younoos as a capable and well-connected candidate. Younoos was formally introduced to party members on Monday.
entries.title: Posters in Mayiladuthurai condemn MP over candidate support

entries.snippet: Ahead of the Tamil Nadu Assembly elections scheduled for April 23, 2026, AIADMK General Secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami (EPS) officially filed his nomination papers. During his campaign, he criticized the ruling DMK government, accusing it of halting several development schemes initiated during the AIADMK’s previous tenure. EPS claimed that the DMK administration has been wasting public funds and promised that all AIADMK-era projects will be resumed if his party is voted back into power. His comments were made during events in Salem and Coimbatore, highlighting the AIADMK's strategy to position itself as a more efficient alternative to the current DMK leadership.
entries.title: Tamil Nadu assembly poll 2026: EPS files papers, accuses DMK govt of wasting public money

entries.snippet: On April 6, 2026, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis criticized the DMK for allegedly halting the traditional lighting of the deepam on Thiruparankundram hill, accusing the party of doing so for vote-bank politics. Speaking in Madurai during his support of BJP candidate Raama Sreenivasan's nomination for the Madurai South constituency, Fadnavis reaffirmed the BJP's commitment to upholding Tamil Nadu's traditions. He voiced confidence in the NDA forming the next state government, attributing this to a shift in public sentiment under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership. Fadnavis also stated that if Sreenivasan is elected, the BJP would work towards extending the metro to Madurai with the PM's support. He leveled serious allegations against the DMK, claiming that 75% of its cabinet leaders face criminal charges and accusing the party of corruption and enabling rising crime rates, particularly in child abuse and drug cases. Additionally, he criticized the DMK's financial mismanagement, citing a state debt exceeding ₹10 lakh crore.
entries.title: Why is DMK stopping Thiruparankundram deepam tradition? asks Fadnavis

entries.snippet: Roshini S, a 28-year-old candidate representing the NTK (Naam Tamilar Katchi) party, is contesting the Tamil Nadu state assembly elections from the Villivakkam constituency in Chennai. She is the only transgender candidate in this election. Roshini’s campaign slogan, "Reach for the skies, Villivakkam (vinnai thodum Villivakkam)," reflects both her political aspirations and personal journey. She emphasizes that the public sees her not merely as a transgender individual, but as a sister figure, suggesting strong community support and acceptance. Her candidacy highlights a move toward greater inclusivity and representation in Tamil Nadu politics.
entries.title: 'People don't see me as a trans candidate, but as a sister': NTK fields Roshini S from Villivakkam in Tamil Nadu polls

entries.snippet: Former MLA M Rajasekaran, representing the AMMK and backed by the NDA, filed his nomination for the Trichy West Assembly constituency. He submitted his papers to RDO and returning officer Salai Dhavalavan. Rajasekaran, originally from Thirupparaithurai, previously won from the now-defunct Thottiyam constituency on a Congress ticket by a slim margin and later contested unsuccessfully from Perambalur in the 2014 (Congress) and 2019 (AMMK) elections. He is set to face incumbent DMK minister K N Nehru in the upcoming election. Rajasekaran was joined by AMMK leaders P Senthilnathan and Sarubala Thondaiman and members from the AIADMK and BJP. On the same day, a total of 24 nominations were submitted across Trichy district's seven constituencies. Trichy East saw the highest number of nominations, including one from TVK leader and actor Vijay. Other filings included TVK's V P Mathiazhagan in Karur and AIADMK's S Divya in Krishnarayapuram.
entries.title: AMMK candidate for Trichy West files nomination

items.snippet:
School Education Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi is contesting for a third consecutive term from the Thiruverumbur assembly constituency, representing the DMK. A sitting MLA since 2016 and a close associate of the party leadership, Mahesh faces a split opposition this time, including AIADMK's former MP P Kumar and TVK’s Navalpattu Viji (alias Vijayakumar), a former DMK member. While Mahesh has historically drawn support from local welfare associations and trade unions in key industrial hubs like BHEL and the Ordnance Factory, this election presents added challenges due to anti-incumbency and internal dissension.

Vijayakumar's entry, especially among youth voters, may fragment votes, though TVK’s internal discontent over his candidacy could limit his impact. NTK's Jallikattu T Rajessh, who polled significantly in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, is also in the fray. Despite Mahesh’s ministerial accomplishments, key promises such as infrastructure upgrades and waste management remain pending. However, with support from Left-leaning unions and urban residents' associations, and his wife Janani Mahesh aiding in rural campaigning, Mahesh remains optimistic about a strong re-election, banking on his government’s broader track record.

entries.snippet: TVK functionary Aadhav Arjuna has accused Chennai City Police Commissioner A Arun of obstructing party leader Vijay's election campaign in the city. Arjuna alleged that the commissioner pressured local officers, resulting in the disruption of planned rallies in Villivakkam, Anna Nagar, and T Nagar. He highlighted a specific incident where police reduced the approved campaign time in T Nagar from 2pm-6pm to only an hour, despite earlier clearance from the Returning Officer. Arjuna criticized the police's role in altering permissions and claimed such interference did not occur in Trichy or Puducherry, where traffic control measures facilitated campaign activities. He also accused the Chennai police of attempting to restrict Vijay to one constituency and prevent him from accessing key urban areas. Describing the commissioner as "dishonest," Arjuna announced TVK’s intention to escalate the matter to the Chief Electoral Officer and potentially the Election Commission in Delhi, demanding fair treatment and public safety from law enforcement. Commissioner Arun did not respond to media inquiries.
entries.title: City commissioner hindering Vijay's rallies, alleges TVK

entries.snippet:
As the nomination deadline for the assembly elections concluded on Monday, candidates from major political parties in the central region of Tamil Nadu actively submitted their nomination papers. In Srirangam, DMK's S Durairaj filed his papers following a procession with party and alliance members. AIADMK's Leema Rose, wife of lottery baron Martin, filed her nomination in Lalgudi. Congress candidate V Lenin Prasad submitted his nomination in the reserved Thuraiyur constituency, accompanied by prominent DMK and Congress leaders. 

In Thiruverumbur, AIADMK's former MP P Kumar and TVK's Navalpattu Viji filed nominations. Pudukkottai district saw nominations from Minister and Thirumayam MLA S Regupathy, Minister Siva Meyyanathan (Alangudi), AIADMK MLA C Vijayabaskar, DMK’s K K Chellapandyan (Viralimalai), and BJP’s Ramachandran (Pudukkottai). In Karur district, DMK candidates from Aravakurichi, Krishnarayapuram, and Kulithalai also filed their nominations. The filings marked the final rush by key candidates across constituencies ahead of the upcoming state assembly elections.
entries.title: Candidates of major parties file papers on last day

entries.snippet:
During a campaign tour across Thanjavur, Perambalur, and Ariyalur districts, Tamil Nadu Deputy Chief Minister Udhayanidhi Stalin criticized AIADMK General Secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami (EPS), sarcastically suggesting that EPS should remain the permanent leader of AIADMK to secure DMK’s electoral victories. Referring to Palaniswami as a “brutal slave,” Udhayanidhi remarked that EPS frequently talks about him, and quipped that it would benefit both DMK and Tamil Nadu if EPS continues leading AIADMK.

Udhayanidhi campaigned in Kunnam for incumbent MLA and Transport Minister S. S. Sivasankar, emphasizing local development. In Thiruvaiyaru, while supporting five-time MLA Durai Chandrasekaran, he urged voters to ensure a larger margin of victory, promising to advocate for Chandrasekaran’s ministerial position if he wins by at least 60,000 to one lakh votes. Udhayanidhi also visited Thiruvidaimaruthur to back incumbent MLA and minister Govi Chezhian.
entries.title: EPS must be permanent AIADMK chief to ensure DMK's win in future: Udhaya

entries.snippet: On Monday, six Members of Parliament from Tamil Nadu took their oaths as Rajya Sabha members. Among them, three are returning MPs: AIADMK's M Thambidurai, PMK's Anbumani Ramadoss, and DMK's Trichy Siva. The newcomers include Congress's Christopher Manickam, DMK's Constantine Ravindran, and DMDK's L K Sudhish. During the oath-taking, Siva, Anbumani, and Constantine Ravindran swore allegiance to values, while Thambidurai, Sudhish, and Manickam took their oaths in the name of God. A moment of contention arose when Sudhish wore his party shawl during the ceremony and was instructed by Vice-President C P Radhakrishnan to remove it. Sudhish also held up a picture of the late DMDK founder Vijayakant during the proceedings.
entries.title: 6 TN MPs take oath in Rajya Sabha

entries.snippet: On April 6, 2026, AIADMK candidate S P Velumani expressed strong confidence in his electoral success in the Thondamuthur constituency for the upcoming Tamil Nadu Assembly election scheduled on April 23. Speaking boldly, Velumani claimed he would secure victory by a margin of at least one lakh votes. This assertion highlights his optimism regarding his support base and campaign momentum in the region.
entries.title: S P Velumani says he will win by one lakh votes in Thondamuthur

entries.snippet: Posters have surfaced in Mayiladuthurai criticizing MP R Sudha for supporting the nomination of Congress candidate Y N Jamal Muhammad Younoos in the upcoming Tamil Nadu assembly elections. Younoos, a 39-year-old from Thanjavur district, has been nominated to contest from the Mayiladuthurai assembly constituency. Local Congress workers expressed dissatisfaction, claiming Younoos is an outsider with no connection or contribution to the constituency or the party locally. The posters, which appeared in places such as bus stands, railway stations, and government buildings, were published under the name of the 'Mayiladuthurai District Congress Committee All Divisions'. They condemned the leadership’s decision to overlook local candidates. Tamil Nadu Congress Committee’s Mayiladuthurai district president, S Bhanusekar, attributed the backlash to a few disgruntled party members, defending Younoos as a capable and well-connected candidate. Younoos was formally introduced to party members on Monday.
entries.title: Posters in Mayiladuthurai condemn MP over candidate support

entries.snippet: Ahead of the Tamil Nadu Assembly elections scheduled for April 23, 2026, AIADMK General Secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami (EPS) officially filed his nomination papers. During his campaign, he criticized the ruling DMK government, accusing it of halting several development schemes initiated during the AIADMK’s previous tenure. EPS claimed that the DMK administration has been wasting public funds and promised that all AIADMK-era projects will be resumed if his party is voted back into power. His comments were made during events in Salem and Coimbatore, highlighting the AIADMK's strategy to position itself as a more efficient alternative to the current DMK leadership.
entries.title: Tamil Nadu assembly poll 2026: EPS files papers, accuses DMK govt of wasting public money

entries.snippet: On April 6, 2026, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis criticized the DMK for allegedly halting the traditional lighting of the deepam on Thiruparankundram hill, accusing the party of doing so for vote-bank politics. Speaking in Madurai during his support of BJP candidate Raama Sreenivasan's nomination for the Madurai South constituency, Fadnavis reaffirmed the BJP's commitment to upholding Tamil Nadu's traditions. He voiced confidence in the NDA forming the next state government, attributing this to a shift in public sentiment under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership. Fadnavis also stated that if Sreenivasan is elected, the BJP would work towards extending the metro to Madurai with the PM's support. He leveled serious allegations against the DMK, claiming that 75% of its cabinet leaders face criminal charges and accusing the party of corruption and enabling rising crime rates, particularly in child abuse and drug cases. Additionally, he criticized the DMK's financial mismanagement, citing a state debt exceeding ₹10 lakh crore.
entries.title: Why is DMK stopping Thiruparankundram deepam tradition? asks Fadnavis

entries.snippet: Roshini S, a 28-year-old candidate representing the NTK (Naam Tamilar Katchi) party, is contesting the Tamil Nadu state assembly elections from the Villivakkam constituency in Chennai. She is the only transgender candidate in this election. Roshini’s campaign slogan, "Reach for the skies, Villivakkam (vinnai thodum Villivakkam)," reflects both her political aspirations and personal journey. She emphasizes that the public sees her not merely as a transgender individual, but as a sister figure, suggesting strong community support and acceptance. Her candidacy highlights a move toward greater inclusivity and representation in Tamil Nadu politics.
entries.title: 'People don't see me as a trans candidate, but as a sister': NTK fields Roshini S from Villivakkam in Tamil Nadu polls

entries.snippet: Former MLA M Rajasekaran, representing the AMMK and backed by the NDA, filed his nomination for the Trichy West Assembly constituency. He submitted his papers to RDO and returning officer Salai Dhavalavan. Rajasekaran, originally from Thirupparaithurai, previously won from the now-defunct Thottiyam constituency on a Congress ticket by a slim margin and later contested unsuccessfully from Perambalur in the 2014 (Congress) and 2019 (AMMK) elections. He is set to face incumbent DMK minister K N Nehru in the upcoming election. Rajasekaran was joined by AMMK leaders P Senthilnathan and Sarubala Thondaiman and members from the AIADMK and BJP. On the same day, a total of 24 nominations were submitted across Trichy district's seven constituencies. Trichy East saw the highest number of nominations, including one from TVK leader and actor Vijay. Other filings included TVK's V P Mathiazhagan in Karur and AIADMK's S Divya in Krishnarayapuram.
entries.title: AMMK candidate for Trichy West files nomination
